facts.text: The diagnostic example advertises interbotix_xs_msgs/JointGroupCommand on the relative commands/joint_group topic and interbotix_xs_msgs/JointSingleCommand on the relative commands/joint_single topic.
The same example subscribes to the relative joint_states topic and hands each sample to a sensor_msgs/JointState callback.
The diagnostic path reads the joint lower and upper limits from the RobotInfo service and builds a sinusoidal joint command around 0 radians, so the group command positions are in radians.
The wx250s motor config declares the joint order [waist, shoulder, elbow, forearm_roll, wrist_angle, wrist_rotate, gripper] and groups the six arm joints as arm.
The X-Series control launch starts the external interbotix_xs_sdk node (or its xs_sdk_sim variant) under the robot_name namespace; the server implementation is not in this clone.
The X-Series README says the packages build on the interbotix_xs_sdk wrapper in the separate interbotix_ros_core repository and directs readers there for implementation details.
The joystick example's torque-off path sets ArmJoy::TORQUE_OFF; this is a message field, not an acknowledged stop service or action.
The joystick example advertises ArmJoy on the relative commands/joy_processed topic.
The diagnostic example's final motion writes Profile_Velocity with set_motor_registers and then publishes a JointGroupCommand carrying the sleep positions; that is another planned motion, not a stop.

safe_state.description: No safe state is claimed: the pinned clone exposes no acknowledged stop service or action, and the external interbotix_xs_sdk owns the motor stop and torque semantics.
